subject: Post-call: Model fit & evals + observed quality regression after update
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
To: Anna Lopez <anna@brightcart.com>
Cc: Ethan Park <ethan_park@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-11-25T09:15:00-08:00
Subject: Post-call recap & recommended next steps (model fit + evals)

Hi Anna —

Thanks for the call this morning — great overview of BrightCart's search-rewrite and product-description workflows. Quick recap and next steps from our side: 

1) Summary of needs:
- High precision on product attribute extraction and canonicalization across noisy user queries
- Low hallucination for product descriptions (especially for long-tail SKUs)
- Budget: production latency target < 200ms p99 and cost sensitivity on high-volume catalog enrichments

2) Recommended models and rationale:
- Llama-2-13B (quant v1) — good balance of precision and cost for structured extractions
- Mistral-7B-instruct — strong on instruction-following for your short prompt pipeline; good for reranking prototypes
- Redwood-llama-13b-compat-v1 (our tuned variant) — lowest hallucination in our retail evals, recommended for initial A/B in production

3) Evals & artifacts I attached:
- brightcart_prompt_set_v1.json — the prompt set we propose to use for continuous evals (includes canonicalization cases and fuzz queries)
- benchmark_summary_sheet.csv — high-level perf/quality snapshot comparing the above variants on your sample data
- Drive link with full eval notebooks in case you'd like to dig deeper: https://drive.google.com/file/d/1a2B_benchmark-summary

4) Next steps / asks:
- We'll run a job this afternoon to run the prompt set across the three recommended variants and share a diffed quality report by EOD.
- If the Redwood-llama-13b-compat-v1 results look good, we can schedule a canary rollout for one collection next week (pinning available for Dedicated).
- Please share any additional edge-case examples you want included in the prompt set (you can reply inline or attach a CSV).

I'll loop Dev and Ethan for model-level questions — thanks again and excited to move this forward.

Best,
Marissa Cole
Enterprise Sales
Redwood Inference

Attachment: brightcart_prompt_set_v1.json (application/json)
Attachment: benchmark_summary_sheet.csv (text/csv)

From: Anna Lopez <anna@brightcart.com>

Cc: BrightCart Ops <ops@brightcart.com>
Date: 2026-11-25T10:42:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Post-call recap & recommended next steps (model fit + evals)

Thanks Marissa — this is exactly the kind of recap that helps. A couple quick notes from the ops team after we ran a few sanity checks against the latest production traffic (we just had the model automatically upgraded last night):

- We observed an uptick in hallucinated attributes for the same prompt set you sent (examples attached inline).
- The reranking precision dropped ~6% on our top-10 product hits; we've attached a small CSV with before/after examples.
- This started immediately after the automatic model update to redwood/llama-13b-quant-v2 (we think the config changed from v1->v2 overnight).

Can you confirm whether you rolled any model updates to our Dedicated pool? If so, we need a path to either pin back to the previous variant or rollback quickly — our merchants are noticing incorrect product titles showing on the site.

Example (before):
- Query: "two-tone sneakers size 9"
- Expected attribute: color=two-tone, size=9
- Model answer (before): correct attributes inserted into structured JSON
- Model answer (after): added bogus "material=leather" attribute, removed size field in some cases

I'll attach the minimal CSV with affected SKUs. Happy to jump on a short call if it helps.

Thanks,
Anna Lopez
Head of Search & Catalog
BrightCart

Attachment: brightcart_regression_examples.csv (text/csv)

From: Dev Patel <dev_patel@redwood.com>

Date: 2026-11-25T13:02:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Post-call recap & recommended next steps (model fit + evals)

Hi all — quick update from the infra/model side after running the prompt set diff against v1 vs v2 on BrightCart's sample: 

Summary:
- We confirmed a measurable quality delta on the prompt_set_v1 across ~2.4k sampled requests: v2 shows +0.08 perplexity and a 5.8% drop in attribute extraction F1 versus v1.
- Root cause appears to be two-fold: quantization changes in the v2 artifact (different kernel ordering) and a change in tokenizer normalization for certain punctuation sequences in the newest tokenizer build.

Recommendation & action plan:
1) Immediate: pin BrightCart Dedicated pool to redwood/llama-13b-compat-v1 (this is the compat variant Marissa recommended) — this will restore prior behavior and can be done within a 10-minute maintenance window. We can do this now if you approve.
2) Short term: roll an internal patch that forces tokenizer normalization to the v1 behavior for your pool; we’ll validate on the prompt set and re-run the benchmark.
3) Long term: add a canary gating rule to prevent automatic upgrades when production-quality delta exceeds threshold for pinned customers.

I attached a short diff extract with the most suspicious operator reorderings: model_diff_patch.txt.

If BrightCart approves the immediate pin, I’ll execute and follow up with the timeline and a post-rollback verification checklist (we’ll run the prompt_set_v1 test again and share error/precision metrics).

Thanks,
Dev Patel
SRE / Inference Infra
Redwood Inference
